recommendations.regimenLabel: Controlled IV BP reduction with a titratable agent
steps: Confirm target-organ damage (distinguishes emergency from urgency).
Controlled IV BP reduction — lower MAP by ~20–25% in the first hour (not to normal), titratable agent (labetalol, nicardipine, GTN).
Tailor target/agent to the syndrome (faster + lower in dissection/pulmonary oedema; cautious in acute stroke).
Identify cause; transition to oral agents once stable.

drugRefs.dose: 20 mg bolus, then 20–80 mg every 10 min, or infusion 0.5–2 mg/min
drugRefs.why: Titratable first-line agent for most hypertensive emergencies; avoid in bradycardia/severe asthma/decompensated heart failure.

drugRefs.dose: 5 mg/h, titrate by 2.5 mg/h every 5–15 min (max 15 mg/h)
drugRefs.why: Smooth, titratable BP control; useful when beta-blockade is contraindicated.
Preferred where there is acute pulmonary oedema or myocardial ischaemia; reduces preload/afterload.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Hypertensive Emergencies
ACC/AHA Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation and Management of High Blood Pressure

confirm: Severe hypertension (often >180/120) WITH acute target-organ damage (encephalopathy, ACS, pulmonary oedema, AKI, retinopathy, dissection).
